plan.hypothesis: On the four-segment v2-T2 configuration, increasing the controller recipe tip-speed weights (holding_tip_speed_weight above its 0.05 nominal and/or terminal_tip_speed_weight raised toward its 0.1 upper bound) will suppress residual tip speed inside the 0.05 s hold window and at target arrival, lowering holding_max_speed and holding_max_error toward the 0.02 m/s and 0.01 m bounds while preserving force bounds and a finite valid execution, moving the joint reach-and-hold outcome toward acceptance without structural change.
plan.rationale: Control-only research is legitimate and the two tip-speed weights are the only legal continuous control paths. The batch source must be distinct from the latest tested entry (v2-T1) and the retained baseline (T0/fixed-radius), so among the remaining complete evidence v2-T2 is the best-supported alternative: it holds the closest terminal error (0.011093 m) and a locally consistent controller-start input and target equilibrium. Coordinate search with fractional step 0.5 probes the weight domain around the recorded nominals (holding 0.05, terminal 0.1) without reapplying any cross-template routing scale; at most two new backend attempts keep the six-execution development budget intact, and every point must produce a complete evaluation with force bounds and a finite valid execution before any claim. The historical T2 values are version9 evidence, so this batch tests them freshly under the fixed controller.gvs_nmpc@10.0.0 rather than assuming transfer.

weakening_observations: Historical executions used controller 9.0.0 (F323) while this batch runs the fixed controller.gvs_nmpc@10.0.0, so historical T2 metrics may not transfer to the new implementation.
No recorded evidence links tip-speed weights to terminal reach; the residual 0.011093 m terminal error (F187) may be structure-limited.
v2-T2 carries split-guide/routing and independent force capacity that confound cross-template attribution.
Held speed 1.121 m/s (F224) is about 56x the 0.02 m/s bound, so one weight change may be insufficient.
The T2 local model shows the target equilibrium as feasible (F561), so its full-run joint failure is not attributable to local static reachability.

decision.reasoning: Feedback first. The retained comparison fixed-radius (T0) reaches terminal 0.00313 m (F145) and holding position 0.00336 m (F284), both inside the 0.01 m bound, but holds at 0.02682 m/s (F28) above the 0.02 m/s bound; its holding_speed component fails (F13) so its status is valid_failure (F127). Its only binding deficiency is held tip speed. The only legal control-only levers here are exactly the two continuous recipe paths control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight and control/recipe/terminal_tip_speed_weight, so speed-weight adaptation is the directly indicated intervention. The batch source must be distinct from both the latest tested entry (v2-T1) and the retained baseline (T0/fixed-radius). Of the remaining complete evidence, v2-T3 (holding speed 3.77 m/s, terminal 0.103 m) is dominated by v2-T2 on every recorded metric, so I branch from v2-T2. T2 is the four-segment template with the closest terminal error (F187 = 0.011093 m), a locally feasible controller-start input for position and braking (F567) and a locally feasible target equilibrium (F561), yet it still fails holding position (F1 = 0.023420 m), holding speed (F224 = 1.121 m/s) and acceptance (F192 = false, F3 = valid_failure) at the recorded nominal weights holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.05 (F497) and terminal_tip_speed_weight = 0.1 (F354). A bounded coordinate search over those two recipe paths tests, under the fixed controller.gvs_nmpc@10.0.0, whether speed-weight adaptation alone can settle the hold window and shave the terminal error. Historical executions ran controller 9.0.0 (F323), so the v10 outcome is not certified by these numbers, hence the uncertain promise.
unresolved_uncertainties: Whether tip-speed weight adaptation on the v2-T2 template actually changes the physical held-window outcome.
Whether the v2-T2 joint failure is structure-limited rather than control-weight-limited.
How far historical controller 9.0.0 metrics transfer to the fixed controller.gvs_nmpc@10.0.0.
